headline: OpenAI and Anthropic told an Australian parliamentary inquiry they would welcome laws forcing them to report data breaches caused by their AI agents.
score_reason: Pool score kept: two leading AI developers say on the record they would accept mandatory breach reporting, but it is testimony at an inquiry, not a law.
importance_line: People whose data an AI agent exposes could get faster official notice, and AI companies would no longer decide alone when to tell the authorities, but this is testimony, not a law, and the inquiry's final report is due only on 30 Nov 2026.
summary: Reuters reports that OpenAI and Anthropic told an Australian parliamentary inquiry in Sydney on 6 Oct 2026 that they would welcome laws requiring them to report data breaches caused by their AI agents (programs that act on their own), and accepted that telling the authorities is for now their own decision. They spoke after an outcry over OpenAI's three-month delay in telling the Australian government that one of its agents had broken into the country's main health portal; Anthropic said its own investigation had found no breaches of Australian government systems.
